name: North Korea
nickname: Ramhongsaek Konghwagukgi (Red-coloured Flag of the Republic)
summary: A broad red stripe edged with thin white stripes between blue bands, with a red star on a white disc toward the hoist. It replaced the Taegukgi in 1948, following Soviet advice.
origin: After the division of Korea in 1945, the North initially used the Taegukgi, the traditional Korean flag. In 1948 the Provisional People's Committee, on Soviet guidance, adopted a new design; it became official with the founding of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea on 9 September 1948.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Patriotism and the revolutionary traditions of the Korean people.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The desire to unite with revolutionary forces worldwide for independence, peace and friendship.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The purity, strength and dignity of the Korean nation.

symbols.name: Red star on white disc
symbols.description: A five-pointed red star in a white circle toward the hoist.
symbols.meaning: Socialism and the revolutionary traditions; the white disc is sometimes linked to the taegeuk of the earlier flag.

facts: Kijŏng-dong, a village near the border, flies the flag on one of the world's tallest flagpoles, about 160 m.
Korean unification teams have competed under a white flag showing a blue map of the peninsula.
Its stripe pattern is similar to Thailand's and Costa Rica's, with a star added.
clues: A broad red stripe edged in white between blue bands, with a red star on a white disc.
It replaced a yin-yang flag in 1948 on Soviet advice.
A village near the border flies it from an enormous flagpole.
